chunks: Ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil from Muyassar said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man bought a skin of oil and found dregs in it. He said: If the buyer is one of those who know that dregs are in the oil, he has no right to return it; and if he is one of those who do not know, he has the right to return it.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on returning oil with dregs if the buyer knew or didn't know about them?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the principle of *gharar* (uncertainty) in sales by linking the right of return (*khiyar al-gharar*) to the buyer's prior knowledge of customary impurities. It establishes that a knowledgeable buyer assumes the risk of typical dregs (*durdī*), whereas an uninformed buyer is protected from hidden defects, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on fairness and transparency in commercial transactions.
